channel.title: Shaping Tomorrow Change Trackers
channel.description: Momentum scans from the Shaping Tomorrow horizon. Each Change Tracker reads across the recent evidence on one topic, labelling the signals beneath it as Accelerating, Stable or Fading, and surfacing the wild cards worth watching.

item.title: Beijing's enforcement hardens; Washington opens a demand-side front
item.description: Third cycle. After June's escalation China's export-control architecture stopped expanding and cools to Stable, while enforcement accelerated via MOFCOM's whole-of-society reporting mechanism and detentions. Washington opened a demand-side front with a 20 July defence-sourcing executive order and on-base stockpiling, and producer-state resource nationalism (the DRC) entered the register as a new accelerating signal.

item.title: Scarcity clears at the cap while the demand behind it faces audit
item.description: Edition 3. The delivery squeeze is now priced: PJM's 2028/29 capacity auction cleared at the FERC-approved $325/MW-day cap with committed supply 6,831 MW short of the reliability requirement, and GE Vernova's gas backlog plus reservations hit 116 GW en route to at least 125 GW under contract by year-end. The counter-current is an audit of demand itself, with Grid Strategies arguing NERC's 90 GW data-centre assumption may be overstated and PJM's monitor tying $23 billion of...

item.title: Europe enacts its simplification; the US stablecoin clock runs down
item.description: Second Change Tracker on Regulation, Standards and Policy Change. Nine signals: 4 Accelerating (EU AI Act deferral and simplification, US GENIUS Act stablecoin rulemaking, EU data-protection simplification, US federal-versus-state AI preemption), 5 Stable (EU sustainability rollback, OECD Pillar Two carve-out, ISSB baseline, US crypto market-structure CLARITY Act, ISO/IEC 42001), 0 Fading. The EU AI Act simplification was formally adopted (Council 29 June), advancing to...

item.title: US and UK stablecoin rulebooks harden as the digital euro clears Parliament
item.category: Financial Services and the Future of Money
item.description: Third Change Tracker on Financial Services and the Future of Money. Nine signals: 6 Accelerating (US stablecoin rulemaking, retail digital euro, UK systemic stablecoin regime, interbank tokenised-deposit clearing, stablecoin deposit disintermediation, agent-initiated machine payments), 2 Stable (wholesale cross-border tokenised settlement, tokenised funds and on-chain MMFs), 1 Fading (cash displacement). The Bank of England systemic stablecoin regime is new to the register...

item.title: US pharma tariffs near enforcement; global health financing retreats
item.category: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
item.description: Second Change Tracker on Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems. Ten signals: 4 Accelerating (US pharma tariffs and MFN pricing, global health financing retrenchment, US vaccine-policy disruption, Medicare GLP-1 access expansion), 5 Stable (EU Critical Medicines Act, antibiotic pipeline shortfall, UK social care workforce reform, AI-designed drug discovery, NHS neighbourhood health shift), 1 Fading (pandemic-preparedness governance). The Section 232 tariff reaches...

item.title: EU migration rules go live as the labour squeeze turns permanent
item.description: Second Change Tracker on Demographics, Migration and Labour Markets. Eight signals: 3 Accelerating (European migration restriction, below-replacement fertility, skilled-talent migration competition), 5 Stable (US net migration, working-age contraction and ageing, retirement-age reform, care and health workforce shortage, AI as a partial demographic offset), 0 Fading. The EU Pact on Migration and Asylum and the Talent Pool regulation both entered into force; two July...

item.title: Drones and capital accelerate; Washington's guarantee thins further
item.description: Edition 2. Counter-drone defence and record private capital lead the accelerators; Ukrainian production scaling into Europe becomes a tracked signal; the US guarantee thins further with a six-month posture review and immediate NATO Force Model cuts; undersea protection cools to Stable.

item.title: Tariff coercion broadens and central-bank gold turns; the dollar erodes only at the edges
item.description: Edition 2. Economic coercion broadens as USTR Section 301 tariffs reach 99.4 percent of US imports and the EU activates its anti-circumvention tool; central-bank gold buying reverses from fading to accelerating, overtaking Treasuries as the largest reserve asset; the dollar reserve share drifts down only gradually while trade reroutes through connector economies.

item.title: Capital repricing arrives as the rulebook stands down
item.description: Cycle 2. AI financing and bubble repricing enters the register as the steepest new mover: a late-June selloff (Nasdaq off over 2%, Micron over 13%) landed with a BIS warning that opaque, circular AI financing could trigger the next crisis. The regulatory brake eased further as the EU gave its AI Act simplification final adoption (29 June) and Colorado's law was stayed and rewritten to a lighter 2027 regime. Capex, agentic adoption and the value-capture gap held Stable as...

item.title: Flattening cuts into the leadership pipeline as layoffs cool
item.description: Cycle 2. Leadership-pipeline erosion enters the register as the steepest new mover: aggressive delayering removes where future leaders are trained, with Gartner projecting one in five firms cutting more than half their middle managers and only 6% of Gen Z wanting senior roles. Layoffs cooled in volume (June down 53%) even as AI became the leading cited reason for cuts and Oracle tied 21,000 to it. Engagement sits at a five-year low of 20% but appears to be bottoming as...

item.title: China blacklists US rare-earth champions as Washington turns market-maker
item.description: Cycle 2. China's 22 June blacklisting of MP Materials and USA Rare Earths flips last cycle's Stable export-control read to Accelerating. Washington deepens its market-maker role through equity stakes, a $110/kg price floor, Section 232 and a $12bn Project Vault stockpile, while allied diversification gained political momentum at the G7 Evian summit yet still trails China's refining grip.

item.title: Delivery overtakes generation as the binding limit; catastrophe momentum cools
item.description: Edition 2. The cycle's dominant movement: delivery, not generation, is now the binding limit. GE Vernova's gas-turbine backlog hit 100 GW with slots booked toward 2030, grid investment still trails over 2,500 GW of stalled queue capacity, and AI data-centre load is the settled premise. Clean supply keeps scaling (renewables past coal in 2025, storage nearing solar) even as US policy compresses the near-term window through the 4 July OBBBA cliff, about USD 2bn of...

item.title: Brussels trims and defers; Washington carves its own track
item.description: Inaugural cycle. The dominant movement is a simplification turn in Europe: the AI Act's high-risk duties are deferred to 2027-2028, the Omnibus I sustainability rollback is in force, and a Digital Omnibus would lighten GDPR. Underneath, multilateral rulebooks splinter into national tracks as the US builds its own stablecoin (GENIUS), tax (Pillar Two carve-out) and AI-preemption rules. Voluntary standards (ISO/IEC 42001, the ISSB disclosures) hold steady as the working...

item.title: Bank clearing layer for tokenised deposits arrives as the digital euro nears a vote
item.category: Financial Services and the Future of Money
item.description: Cycle 2. A shared interbank clearing layer for tokenised deposits, a cycle-one wild card, becomes a live programme via The Clearing House; cross-border tokenised settlement and tokenised funds keep advancing; the retail digital euro moves from Stable to Accelerating ahead of a committee vote; the stablecoin deposit-flight evidence stays contested.

item.title: Tariff and pricing shocks accelerate; pandemic governance stalls
item.category: Health, Life Sciences and Care Systems
item.description: Inaugural cycle. The momentum sits in policy and trade: a US Section 232 pharmaceutical tariff and most-favored-nation pricing regime, the EU Critical Medicines Act and a Medicare GLP-1 access push lead the accelerators, while multilateral pandemic-preparedness governance fades as the WHO pathogen-sharing annex slips to 2027 and the antibiotic pipeline keeps thinning.

item.title: Washington reroutes its tariff weapon as the dollar order erodes
item.description: Inaugural Change Tracker on Geopolitics and Economic Fragmentation. Eight signals: 4 Accelerating (US tariff regime after the IEEPA ruling, sanctions and economic statecraft escalation, alternative payment infrastructure, friend-shoring and trade rerouting), 3 Stable (bloc-aligned trade reconfiguration, declining dollar reserve share, fragmentation drag on global growth), 1 Fading (central-bank gold accumulation). Three wild cards: a Section 301 uncapped tariff war, a...

item.title: The execution layer goes live as the rulebook stands down
item.description: Inaugural Change Tracker on Artificial Intelligence and Automation. Eight signals: 5 Accelerating (agentic AI to production, AI capex supercycle, open-weight frontier parity, EU AI Act delay via the Digital Omnibus, US pre-emption of state AI law), 2 Stable (AI data-centre power demand, enterprise value-capture gap), 1 Fading (AI-driven entry-level labour squeeze, as the displacement narrative is walked back). Three wild cards: AI infrastructure repricing, autonomous agent...

item.title: Layers fall and offices fill as engagement hits a new floor
item.description: Inaugural Change Tracker on Workforce, Skills and Organisational Change. Eight signals: 5 Accelerating (the Great Flattening of middle management, white-collar forever layoffs, manager and employee engagement collapse, five-day return-to-office mandates, AI agents entering the org as coworkers), 2 Stable (reskilling imperative and shortening skill half-life, skills-based hiring policy-practice gap), 1 Fading (AI-driven entry-level hiring squeeze, as the displacement...

item.title: Reserves and rails are reorganising faster than the rulebooks
item.category: Fragmentation of the Global Financial System
item.description: Inaugural Change Tracker on global financial fragmentation. Eight signals tracked: 5 Accelerating (BRICS Pay/mBridge, Project Agora, gold reserves, panda bonds, regulatory perimeter divergence), 3 Stable (OFAC/REPO Act, FSB/IMF/BIS coordination, dollar reserve share). Two wild cards: kinetic attacks on financial AI infrastructure, AI-Native centres as new bridge category.

item.title: The bar is being reshaped from three directions at once
item.description: Inaugural Change Tracker on Danish law firms for Dreyers Fond. Eight signals: 6 Accelerating (firm-wide AI deployment at Kromann Reumert, EU AI Act compliance, young-lawyer priority shift, international/pan-Nordic firm presence, Bar Council bylaw renewal, legal-tech vendor maturity), 2 Stable (IBA Copenhagen 2026, specialisation/boutique consolidation). Two wild cards: AI Act enforcement event, pan-Nordic merger of a Danish top-five.

item.title: Power demand outpaces grid; US policy retreats; insured losses harden
item.description: Inaugural cycle. Clean build-out is accelerating with renewables, batteries crossing the 100 GW annual-additions mark and the first US advanced-nuclear construction permit in roughly a decade; AI-driven data-centre load and PJM price escalation strain firm capacity even as 2.6 TW sits in the interconnection queue; OBBBA's IRA rollback and the offshore-wind retreat compress US clean-energy capex into a 2026-2027 window; a sixth consecutive USD 100 bn-plus insured-loss year...

item.title: State intervention in critical minerals accelerates as the export-control truce holds
item.description: Inaugural cycle. Government intervention dominates the momentum: US strategic stockpiling, equity stakes, price floors and Section 232 trade remedies are accelerating alongside China's new supply-chain security law, while the acute 2025 export-control weapons sit paused under a US-China truce and minor-metals curbs ease.

item.title: Stablecoin rules harden as tokenised bank money scales and cash plateaus
item.category: Financial Services and the Future of Money
item.description: Inaugural cycle. United States GENIUS Act rulemaking and a maturing tokenised settlement stack lead the accelerators; the retail digital euro holds a steady multi-year tempo and the cash-displacement story has plateaued.
